newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Over 200 rebels dead, wounded in Sri Lanka battle.
newsitem.headline: Over 200 rebels dead, wounded in Sri Lanka battle.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops killed or wounded more than 200 Tamil Tiger rebels in their first major push against the guerrillas in more than a month, a military spokesman said on Monday.
But the rebels put up a stiff fight against troops who on Sunday advanced on their northern Kilinochchi stronghold, backed by tanks, artillery and air support, military officials said.
"Our troops are digging in in the newly-captured area three km from Kilinochchi," a military spokesman said. "We met heavy resistance."
The rebels struck in the east on Monday, ambushing an army patrol in Batticaloa and killing five soldiers, he said.
Western aid workers said their teams near the battleground had reported that heavy shelling and bombing heard since Sunday had stopped by Monday evening.

The military spokesman said ground troops and rebel radio transmissions intercepted by the army indicated more than 200 casualties among the Tigers in Sunday's action, but he was unable to say how many had been killed.
Military officials said at least 30 soldiers had been killed in fierce fighting around Kilinochchi by noon on Monday.
The spokesman said on Sunday alone one officer and 21 soldiers were killed and 58 wounded.
Defence analysts said government troops tried to outflank Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels who were well dug in at Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.

It was the first major push in more than a month by security forces who had consolidated at the road junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, a gateway to the rebels' jungle territory of the Wanni.
"Domination of areas well ahead of Paranthan defences by security forces started early Sunday," the spokesman said.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, accused the troops of attacking civilians.
"The armed forces are directing their attack on civilian concentrations which are scattered around the intended path of the army's advance," it said in a statement.
Most of an estimated 150,000 people in Kilinochchi have evacuated the town since the military first launched its offensive in July but many still live on the outskirts.
The LTTE set up a base at Kilinochchi in April after the army captured the northern Jaffna peninsula, which the LTTE had ruled for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.
Jaffna is now separated from the government-held mainland by a big chunk of rebel territory that reaches from Kilinochchi to Vavuniya, 70 km (44 miles) to the south.
The army has said it wants to reopen the main highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through the Wanni, to reduce dependence on air and sea routes.
The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.
It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.
